name: Plumb the Forbidden
oracle_text:
As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice one or more creatures. When you do, copy this spell for each creature sacrificed this way.
You draw a card and lose 1 life.
blocked_sentences: As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice one or more creatures. When you do, copy this spell for each creature sacrificed this way.

needs.what: A card-level field holding an *optional, non-mana, variable-count* additional cost paid as the spell is cast from hand: a full `Cost` whose `sacrifice` selector (`{"types": ["Creature"], "controller": "you"}`) takes *any number the caster chooses, including zero*, charged at cast time alongside the printed {1}{B}. Two things beyond deadly_dispute's mandatory version: the payment must be offered rather than required (the spell is legal with no creatures at all), and the count must be player-chosen at cast time rather than fixed by the selector's `count`, so the caster picks a set of creatures and the whole set is sacrificed as one payment while the spell goes on the stack.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `kicker` is the only additional cost a hand-cast spell can carry, and it is mana-only -- `CardDef.kicker` is a mana-cost *string* and the cast variant is `mana_cost.plus(kicker)`, a `ManaCost`, so it cannot sacrifice anything. `Cost.sacrifice` (in `carddef.py`) is exactly the right shape but is only reachable from an activated ability's `cost` or from a graveyard-cast path (`flashback`/`graveyard_cost`/`retrace`), never from an ordinary cast from hand; it is also a single fixed selector, so even mounted on a spell it would demand exactly N creatures rather than "one or more, your choice how many". Moving the sacrifice into `spell_effects` with the `sacrifice` op is the approximation the DSL notes forbid: it pays on resolution, which makes the copies impossible to have made (they must already be on the stack) and lets the spell be cast with the sacrifice unpaid.

needs.what: A "When you do, ..." reflexive trigger on a spell: an ability attached to an *optional cost or optional action* that triggers only when that option was actually taken, resolves before the spell it belongs to, and carries bindings from the payment. Here it must fire as Plumb the Forbidden is cast (creatures were sacrificed), put its `copy_spell` on the stack above the original, and not fire at all when zero creatures were sacrificed.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: No event in `trigger_events` observes a cost being paid. `spell_cast` fires for the whole cast and cannot tell whether the optional additional cost was taken, and it is a normal trigger that goes on the stack independently rather than a reflexive one bound to the payment. The `kicked` condition in `condition_keys` is the nearest read-back of an optional cost, but it is a *resolution-time* `if` inside `spell_effects` -- by the time a `{"if": {"kicked": true}}` runs, the spell is already the top of the stack resolving, so a `copy_spell` from there would copy a spell that is no longer copyable in the way rule 706.10 wants and would resolve after, not before, the original. `creature_dies`/`dies` do fire from the sacrifice, but they are per-creature triggers on the creatures, not on the spell, and cannot distinguish creatures sacrificed to pay this cost from any other death.

needs.what: A value expression for "the number of permanents sacrificed to pay this spell's additional cost", available to the reflexive trigger's effects so `copy_spell`'s `amount` can be that count. The payment must record how many objects it consumed and expose them as a binding on the trigger.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `value_keys` has no reading of what a cost consumed. `creatures_died_this_turn` is the closest, and it is wrong: it counts every creature that died this turn from any source -- combat, an earlier removal spell, a second Plumb the Forbidden -- so on a real board it would copy the spell too many times. `creatures_you_control` counts what survives, not what was paid. `count` over a selector cannot name "the ones sacrificed this way" because nothing marks them.

notes: The second line, "You draw a card and lose 1 life", is fully expressible today as `draw` for one plus `lose_life` for one, and `copy_spell` already ships, so this card needs only the cast-time machinery. It shares the `additional_cost` capability with data/authoring/gaps/deadly_dispute.json but demands strictly more of it: deadly_dispute's cost is mandatory and fixed at one permanent, this one is optional and variable, and only this one needs the payment's size read back. Building the optional variable form covers the mandatory fixed form, and the same pair of capabilities unblocks casualty and replicate, which docs/keywords.md already records as waiting on "an additional cost".
